players.product: EDA software and chip design simulation tools accelerated by NVIDIA CUDA

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2026 results: revenue of $2.41 billion at the high end of guidance, mainly on the timing of Ansys deals; Ansys revenue approximately $886 million (its seasonally strong December quarter fell into Synopsys' Q1); non-GAAP operating margin 42.1%; non-GAAP EPS $3.77, above guidance; backlog ended at $11.3 billion. Design Automation segment revenue approximately $2 billion (adjusted operating margin 47.3%), with strong growth in hardware-assisted verification partly offset by the Optical Solutions Group divestiture. Free cash flow approximately $822 million; the entire $4.3 billion term loan repaid.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue $2.41 billion; Ansys ~$886 million; non-GAAP OM 42.1%; non-GAAP EPS $3.77; backlog $11.3 billion; Design Automation ~$2 billion (47.3% adj. OM)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance: revenue, non-GAAP operating margin and cash-flow targets reiterated and non-GAAP EPS raised. Full-year revenue $9.56 billion to $9.66 billion, Ansys contribution $2.9 billion at the midpoint (growing double digits), non-GAAP operating margin 40.5% at the midpoint, non-GAAP EPS $14.38 to $14.46 (up $0.06), CapEx approximately $300 million, free cash flow approximately $1.9 billion. Q2 revenue target $2.225 billion to $2.275 billion with non-GAAP EPS $3.11 to $3.17. The Board authorized repurchases of up to $2 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: FY26 revenue $9.56 billion to $9.66 billion; non-GAAP EPS $14.38 to $14.46; FCF ~$1.9 billion; Q2 revenue $2.225 billion to $2.275 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO described 'a tale of 2 markets': the multibillion-dollar AI infrastructure build-out 'continues unabated', driving system-level and semiconductor R&D with robust design-start activity for AI compute, while design starts in consumer, automotive and industrial remain subdued despite signals of modest recovery. China headwinds persist: China grew approximately 21% only because of Ansys; excluding Ansys, China revenue declined slightly, as cumulative entity-list and technology restrictions hit demand (IP most, as some Chinese customers turn to domestic foundries), and domestic competitors are appearing where customers cannot use Synopsys technology and look for alternatives.
quarterly_data.figure: China ~21% growth incl. Ansys; China ex-Ansys declined slightly

quarterly_data.signal: Hardware and AI-driven EDA: a marquee emulation win versus the incumbent at a leading AI HPC customer; hardware (ZeBu, HAPS and the hybrid EP emulation-prototyping family) had a record year last year and is expected to keep delivering given customer design complexity. Major semi and hyperscale customers using Synopsys.ai have seen up to 50% faster knowledge assistance, up to 70% faster workflow assistance and up to 5x faster formal test bench generation, with several agent-engineer engagements underway in design and verification (early focus on the front end). The digital flow (Fusion Compiler and PrimeTime) achieved 100% usage on critical tape-outs at 2-nanometer and below.
quarterly_data.figure: Synopsys.ai up to 50% / 70% / 5x faster; Fusion Compiler + PrimeTime 100% usage on critical tape-outs at 2-nanometer and below

quarterly_data.signal: Ansys integration: first wave of joint Synopsys + Ansys solutions (bringing physics analysis such as thermal and structural into multi-die design) to be delivered in the first half of FY26, with monetization expected to start in FY27. Commitments are $400 million revenue-synergy run rate by year 4 and $400 million cost-synergy run rate by year 3 (being accelerated into 2026). Long-term growth view unchanged: EDA double digits, IP mid-teens, simulation and analysis double digits.
quarterly_data.figure: $400 million revenue synergies run rate by year 4; $400 million cost synergies run rate by year 3

contracts.signal: CEO called the recently announced NVIDIA partnership 'not a press release partnership' but a deep commitment from both companies. Layer one: a joint R&D road map porting Synopsys EDA and legacy Ansys products to GPU acceleration, with a number of them expected to be delivered in '26 as parallel GPU versions priced for the value uplift. Layer two: Omniverse digital twins for physical AI, where Ansys simulation and analysis supplies the accuracy.
contracts.date_signed: not stated (recently announced as of Q1 FY2026)
contracts.type: strategic partnership / joint R&D (GPU-accelerated EDA and simulation)

players.product: 3DIC Compiler multi-die / advanced-package design-to-signoff platform used to deliver Instinct MI455X

quarterly_data.signal: Multi-die momentum accelerated as leading semiconductor and foundry customers adopted the 3DIC Compiler platform, which pairs automation and AI-driven optimization with Synopsys' multiphysics analysis tools to improve signal and power integrity, thermal efficiency and design convergence. AI-build-out customers are 'racing to deploy' Synopsys.ai, 3DIC Compiler, Fusion Compiler, PrimeTime and VCS.

connects_to.relationship: multi-die / advanced-package design and sign-off platform (3DIC Compiler) used to deliver the Instinct MI455X GPU; joint autonomous EDA workflow work with AMD and Microsoft

contracts.signal: Synopsys received World Economic Forum honors for its work with AMD to advance AI-accelerated chip design.

players.product: Semiconductor IP (interface / foundation IP) supplied to ASIC design houses under an IP OEM partnership (Gaonchips supplier)

quarterly_data.signal: Design IP revenue was $407 million, down approximately 6% year-over-year and flat sequentially, with adjusted operating margin of 16.2%. Management called FY26 a transitional year for IP with muted growth and sequential improvement, weighted to Q4 as schedule work on a few IP titles is completed (titles high-end HPC customers need include PCIe, 224 SerDes, HBM, LPDDR and UCIe), with monetization toward the latter part of the year; IP margin stays compressed this year because investment is unchanged.
quarterly_data.figure: Design IP $407 million, down ~6% YoY, flat QoQ; adj. OM 16.2%

quarterly_data.signal: Interconnect IP: more than 40 PCIe design wins in the quarter with HPC and automotive customers, an industry-first demonstration of PCIe 8.0, and a first-to-market 224 gig SerDes on advanced nodes and leading foundries with 10 lifetime wins. Interconnect standards now turn over in about half the historical 3-to-4-year life. Hyperscalers, which lack their own IP teams, want customized IP delivered 'one generation ahead'; Synopsys is in active talks and expects several to become actual business in FY26, with the upside arriving after customer tape-outs.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 40 PCIe design wins; 224 gig SerDes 10 lifetime wins

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio refocus: the planned sale of the processor IP (ARC) business to GlobalFoundries narrows the IP focus to interconnect and foundation IP, where management sees the bigger growth opportunity (many customers now design their own processors with Synopsys EDA). ARC stays in the financials until the deal closes, and its size was not disclosed. The CEO said GF would be a partner on both the interface IP and EDA sides with joint customers.
